The first mosque on earth was al-Masjid al-Haram, then al-Aqsa forty years later, and wherever the time of prayer comes, the earth is a mosque.
Arriving in Medina, the Prophet prayed in sheepfolds until the Banu al-Najjar gave their land for Allah's reward and he had it cleared to build the mosque.
The Prophet called builders of places of worship on pious men's graves the worst of creatures, cursed Jews and Christians who took their prophets' graves as mosques, and forbade it.
When people objected to Uthman rebuilding the Prophet's mosque, he cited the Prophet: whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah builds for him a house like it in Paradise.
The Prophet scraped spittle off the qibla wall and told worshippers to spit only left, under the foot; spitting in the mosque is a sin, expiated by burying it.
Whoever eats garlic, onion or leek should keep away from the mosque, for the smell harms angels and people, though the Prophet would not forbid what Allah made lawful.
One who hears a man calling out in the mosque for something lost should say, May Allah not restore it to you, for mosques were not built for this.
The Prophet prayed in blind Itban's house to mark a prayer place for him, and there said Allah forbids the Fire to whoever declares His oneness seeking His pleasure.
Walking far to prayer brings greater reward; the Prophet told a distant Ansari and Banu Salama their steps were recorded, each erasing a sin or raising a degree.
Whoever goes to the mosque in the morning or evening, Allah prepares a feast for him in Paradise each morning or evening.
The places dearest to Allah are the mosques and the most hateful to Him are the markets.
Entering the mosque one asks Allah to open the doors of His mercy and prays two rak'ahs before sitting, as the Prophet told Jabir and did after journeys.
Prayer in the Prophet's mosque is better than a thousand elsewhere except the Sacred Mosque; Maimuna told a woman who vowed to pray in Bait al-Maqdis to pray there instead.
Journeys are undertaken only to three mosques, the Sacred Mosque, the Prophet's and al-Aqsa, and the mosque founded on piety is the Prophet's mosque in Medina.
The Prophet came to Quba, riding or on foot, every Saturday and prayed two rak'ahs in its mosque, and Ibn Umar did the same.
When people objected to Uthman rebuilding the Prophet's mosque, he cited the Prophet: whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah builds him a house in Paradise.
